with Terminal Alkynes and Organozinc Reagents. A General Route to ~-Substituted Butenolides

Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, 
Chinese Academy of Sciences, 354 Fenglin Lu, Shanghai 200032, People's Republic of China 
Received 5 May 1999; revised 21 July 1999; accepted 12 August 1999 
Abstract: An improved procedure for the efficient synthesis of I~-halobutenolides was developed. The Pd(0)- 
catalyzed coupling reactions of 13-halobutenolides with terminal alkynes or organozinc reagents, i.e., 1-alkenyl, 
aryl, and alkyl zinc reagents, to afford 13-substituted butenolides were carefully studied. Using the coupling 
protocol of T-(n-butyl)-13-iodobutenolide with methylzinc halide, we performed an efficient formal synthesis of 
whisky lactone. © 1999 Elsevier Science Ltd. All rights reserved. 
Introduction 
Recently much attention has been paid to the synthesis of butenolides with different substitution patterns 
due to their potential biological activities. Butenolide-containing compounds are considered as potential 
insecticides, bactericides, fungicides, antibiotics, anticancer agents, anti-inflammatories, allergy inhibitors, 
antisoriasis agents, cyclooxygenase inhibitors, and phospholipase A2 inhibitors, etc. ~ Recently, we developed a 
Pd(0)/Ag+-cocatalyzed one-step methodology for the efficient synthesis ofbutenolides starting from 1,2-allenic 
carboxylic acids and organic halides (eq. 1). 2

Pd(0)/Cul-Coeatalyzed Sonogashira Coupling Reactions of 13-Elalobutenolides with Terminal Alkynes. 
Sonogashira coupling reaction s has been developed as one of the most powerful tools for the synthesis of 
disubstituted alkynes. We tested the coupling reaction ofv-(n-butyl)-J3-iodobutenolide 2a with phenylacatylene 
using Et3N as the base and TI-W or CH3CN as the solvent. Under the catalysis of PdCI2(PPh3)2 and CuI, the 
coupling reaction did occur, but the yield was poor (-42%). Here, probably the instability of 13-iodobutenolide 
2a towards EhN might be the reason for a low-yielding reaction. Under Sonogashira's original conditions, i.e., 
using Et3N as both the solvent and the base, the yield was 67%. If the coupling reaction was carried out in 
DMF, the yield was similar (66%). However, after further screening we found that when K2CO3 was used in 
place of EhN as the base, the coupling product 3a was formed cleanly in CH3CN and isolated in 99% yield 
(entry 1, Table 1).

the catalysis of Pd(PPh3)4, [3-halobutenolides can cross-couple with aryl or alkenyl zinc reagents. 7,s Some

prepared efficiently via the transmetalation reaction of ZnBr2 with aromatic lithiums, which were prepared by 
the halogen-lithium exchange reactions of the corresponding aromatic halides with n-BuLi. 9 The subsequent 
coupling reaction went smoothly with TI-W as the solvent (entries 1, 2, and 3, Table 2); (2) vinylzine bromide 
was prepared by the transrnetalation reaction of vinylmagnesium bromide with ZnBr2, while (E)-1-hexenylzinc 
bromide was prepared from (E)-l-hexenyl iodide by its treatment with n-BuLl followed the addition of ZnBr2. 
The reaction was heterogeneous and did not occur in pure TIlT (entry 5, Table 2). However, with the addition 
of DMF as the cosolvent, the coupling reaction was homogeneous and afforded the fl-vinyl butenolides 4 in 
moderate to goodyields (entries 4, 6, and 7, Table 2); (3) 7-(n-butyl)-13-bromobutenolide 2c also coupled with 
vinylzinc bromide to afford 4e (entry 8, Table 2).
